Upper bound lemmas proved: (i) sorted-multiset reduction is complete because zero-sum is order-independent and sorting breaks n! symmetry; zero excluded correctly because singleton 0 is zero-sum. (ii) Incremental test -g in M is exact for g!=0: new zero-sums must use g as 0=s+g, and prefix zero-sum-free implies 0 only via empty, so test is both necessary and sufficient; pruned branches all contain same witness so safe. Code audit of enumerate.c: 54-bit mask in uint64_t, addtab/negtab built as (a+a2)%3 etc. correct, extend_mask = mask OR {s+g}, dfs over nondecreasing indices from 1..53 enumerates each multiset once. originality.rationale: Live retrieval defeats novelty. Nearest prior Bhowmik & Schlage-Puchta (2007) 'Davenport's constant for groups of the form Z3(+)Z3(+)Z_{3d}', CRM Proc. 43 pp.307-326, DOI 10.1090/crmp/043/17, studies the exact infinite family containing the candidate: d=2 gives Z3xZ3xZ6. Biswas & Mazumdar arXiv:2402.09999 (2024, published Math Notes 118:23-34, 2025) 'Davenport constant for finite abelian groups with higher rank', which itself studies G=(Cp)^{d-1}xC_{pq} (p=3,q=2,d=3 is exactly the candidate), states verbatim 'It is already known that D(G)=D*(G) for the groups C3xC3xC_{3s} for any positive integer s ([BP2])' where [BP2] is Bhowmik 2007. With s=2, C3xC3xC_{6} has D*=10, i.e. exactly the candidate theorem D=10=D*. DRAFT Sec.6 omits this family, listing only Olson p-groups, rank-two formula, surveys, and EGZ rank<=2, and claims 'no citable exact entry' and 'flagged open' and 'first certified exact' — false in light of the 2007 family result as summarized in 2024-2025 literature. Substantive comparison: same group, same invariant, same equality D=D*=10 with same canonical witness type; candidate's 84.9M-node DFS is at most an independent recomputation, not a new object, gap, or method. Therefore originality FAIL.

value.rationale: Counterfactually, if new, an exact Davenport value for a rank-3 mixed group with explicit length-9 witness, full 511-row verification table, and replayable complete length-10 exhaustion in seconds would be independently worth finding later: recognized Davenport/EGZ invariant citable for zero-sum and factorization benchmarks, structural rank-preserving choice (only n=6 preserves rank 3 vs. collapsing siblings C3xC21/C3xC24), not a textbook D* restatement alone (non-textbook direction D<=10 proved), not a mere parameter slide within rank-two formula, not a tiny unmotivated gain (closes exact constant, not bound by 1), and explained enumeration with pruning lemmas and single-command replay, not unexplained. Hence value PASS as a result type; overall REJECT still follows from originality failure.

sources.comparison: Zakarczemny derives a generic rank-three upper bound D<=D*+(a3-3)(n1-1) with a3<=20369, which for C3xC3xC6 is astronomically slack; this shows generic rank-three bounds do not close the entry and closure must come from family-specific theorems like Bhowmik's, which already exists for this family.

residual_risks: Upper bound has no DRAT/proof-assistant certificate; rests on ~116-line C program correctness, but mitigated by tiny auditable source, two-lemma proof, independent brute cross-checks, and bit-for-bit rerun.

Bhowmik 2007 full text is paywalled (AMS login wall); decisive 'any s' generality is evidenced via Biswas 2024 PDF text and Springer reference list rather than direct Bhowmik theorem-line inspection, but title-family match (Z3xZ3xZ_{3d} with d=2) plus explicit secondary assertion makes misattribution risk low.
Computational re-proof remains correct and replayable, but as a replication of a 2007 exact value it is not independently publishable as a new constant.
